note: Approximate, indicative reconstructions of lost/shifted rivers and former lakes, hand-traced from published studies. Each feature carries fromYear/toYear (the era it existed) for time-enabled display. NOT survey-accurate.

properties.name: Sarasvati (Ghaggar-Hakra)
properties.note: The great river of the Harappan civilisation; dried as the monsoon weakened and tributaries shifted.

properties.name: Tamanrasset (Green Sahara river)
properties.note: A Ganges-sized river that crossed a green Sahara to the Atlantic; dried as the African Humid Period ended.

properties.name: Nile — Ahramat branch
properties.note: A long-lost arm of the Nile that flowed past ~31 pyramids (Giza to Lisht); silted up by ~1000 BC.
properties.source: Ghoneim et al. 2024, Communications Earth & Environment

properties.name: Nile — Pelusiac branch
properties.note: The easternmost ancient Nile distributary, guarding Egypt's frontier at Pelusium; silted in the medieval period.

properties.name: Yellow River — southern course
properties.note: For ~700 years after the 1128 avulsion the Huang He flowed SOUTH, merging with the Huai into the Yellow Sea.

properties.name: Amu Darya — Uzboy channel
properties.note: The Oxus periodically spilled west down the Uzboy channel to the Caspian Sea until ~1600 AD.

properties.name: Channel River (Fleuve Manche)
properties.note: A vast Ice-Age river draining the Rhine, Thames and Seine down the dry English Channel to the Atlantic.

properties.name: Po (Adriatic plain)
properties.note: The Po ran far across the exposed northern Adriatic plain to reach the sea near today's mid-Adriatic.

properties.name: Hudson (shelf valley)
properties.note: At low sea level the Hudson crossed the exposed Atlantic shelf to a canyon at the shelf edge.

properties.name: Lake Mega-Chad
properties.note: Once one of the world's largest lakes (~Caspian-sized); shrank to today's small Lake Chad as the Sahara dried.

properties.name: Lop Nur
properties.note: Terminal lake of the Tarim basin; wandered and shrank, finally drying in the 20th century.

properties.name: Lake Moeris (Fayum)
properties.note: A great freshwater lake in the Fayum, central to ancient Egyptian life; shrank to today's Birket Qarun.

properties.name: Aral Sea (former extent)
properties.note: The world's 4th-largest lake until Soviet irrigation drained it from the 1960s onward.

properties.name: Lake Agassiz
properties.note: A colossal glacial lake from the melting Laurentide ice sheet; its sudden drainage (~6200 BC) likely chilled the climate and helped drown Doggerland.

properties.name: Lake Bonneville
properties.note: A vast Ice-Age lake in the Great Basin; the Great Salt Lake is its shrunken remnant.

properties.name: Lake Lahontan
properties.note: A large pluvial lake across northwestern Nevada during the last Ice Age.

properties.name: Khvalynian Caspian (giant Caspian)
properties.note: The Caspian swelled far beyond today's shores after glacial meltwater poured in, even spilling toward the Black Sea.

properties.name: West Siberian Lake (Mansi)
properties.note: An immense ice-dammed lake ponded across the West Siberian Plain when ice blocked the north-flowing rivers.

properties.name: Black Sea (freshwater lake)
properties.note: Before ~5600 BC the Black Sea was a smaller freshwater lake; the Mediterranean then broke through the Bosporus (the proposed 'Black Sea deluge').
properties.source: Ryan & Pitman, Black Sea deluge hypothesis

properties.name: Lake Carpentaria
properties.note: A large freshwater lake in the Gulf of Carpentaria when it was cut off from the sea on the exposed Sahul shelf.
